## Spatial units: eco-stratification

![](images/eco-strata/black_spruce_nested_strata_volume_curves.png){fig-align="center"}

::: notes
Example for black spruce and total volume, illustrating how the hierarchy works.
From the ecozone level (e.g., Boreal Plains) down to ecoprovince (Boreal Foothills),
ecoregion (Western Alberta Upland) and the individual ecodistricts. Curves become
increasingly spatially specific, and separate more at finer levels. More detailed
does not automatically mean better.
:::

## Model library overview

- Forest attribute: AGB, total volume

- Species-specific or multi-species (Generic  →  Conifer / Broadleaf  →  Species)

- Spatial representation: Tile, Ecozone → Ecoprovince → Ecoregion → Ecodistrict

- Model formulation: National, Regional

- Uncertainty

::: notes
Two response variables; different levels of biological specificity; tiles plus the
nested ecological hierarchy; national and regional formulations.
:::

::: notes
The release contains 27,208 catalogue rows, of which package prediction functions use
the 17,292 national curves. Regional-fit records preserve development provenance and
comparison evidence. Ecological models are limited to the 12 forested ecozones.
:::
